Definition: from G3844 and G2749; to lie near, i.e. be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy):--be present.
BiblicalUsage: Parakeimai means to lie near, to be at hand, present with. Paul says, I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwelleth no good thing, for to will is present with me, but how to perform that which is good I find not.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this one verse names the believer's daily war: the will to do good lies close at hand, and the power to do it does not, until Christ supplies it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
